result.target_topic: Human Capital and Leadership Transition Risks
result.target_summary: Intel faces intense competition for skilled talent, with demand exceeding supply, and risks from immigration policies and remote work trends. Stock price declines have reduced the value of share-based awards, hindering retention. Additionally, changes in senior leadership, including the retirement of the CEO in December 2024, pose risks of disruption due to the long development cycles and large capital investments inherent in semiconductor manufacturing. Effective hiring, onboarding, and retention of key employees and leadership are critical to mitigating these risks.

peer_results.rationale: The provided AMD candidates concern inventory valuation methodology and operating loss breakdowns, which are financial accounting topics unrelated to the target's topic of human capital competition, leadership transition risks, and equity-based compensation retention strategies.

comparisons.peer_summary: The company approved a broad-based program of multi-year equity grants of time- and market-based RSUs in the first quarter of fiscal year 2019, which vest on the same basis as four annual grants made on March 15 of each year with successive four-year vesting periods, with expense recognized from grant date through vesting over a range of 4 to 7 years.
comparisons.comparison: Both Intel and Broadcom disclose the use of multi-year equity awards as a key component of their compensation strategies to attract and retain talent, though they differ in structure and timing. Intel highlights that sustained declines in its stock price have reduced the retention value of these awards, impacting competitiveness, while Broadcom details a specific broad-based program approved in 2019 involving time- and market-based RSUs that vest over successive four-year periods, with expenses recognized over 4 to 7 years.

sentences.text: To help attract, retain, and motivate qualified employees, we use share-based awards, such as RSUs, and performance-based cash incentive awards.

Sustained declines in our stock price or lower stock price performance relative to our competitors have reduced the retention value of our share-based awards, which can impact the competitiveness of our compensation.

During the first quarter of fiscal year ended November 3, 2019 ("fiscal year 2019"), our Compensation Committee approved a broad-based program of multi-year equity grants of time- and market-based RSUs (the "Multi-Year Equity Awards") in lieu of our annual employee equity awards historically granted on March 15 of each year.
We recognize stock-based compensation expense related to the Multi-Year Equity Awards from the grant date through their respective vesting date, ranging from 4 years to 7 years.
